PT-121,Uma,Desai,strong,,,none,,85,,Cooking with my dad on weekends taught me that recipes are just instructions you can argue with. I redid the wrist routine three times because the first version hurt and the third version finally felt right.
PT-122,Victor,Chen,improving,"Speech-language follow-up — post-stroke",MRN-2026-1006,none,,62,,People talk fast in the waiting room and I catch every third word. In the exercises I can take my time and do exactly what I mean. This balance set took me four tries and I think that is okay.
PT-123,Willa,Anderson,strong,,,none,,91,,"My horse Scout got colic in January and I was on my feet in the barn all night. I wrote in my log about how fear feels like cold hands. Scout is fine now. My hip held up through the whole thing, which is my proudest win."
PT-124,Xavier,Thompson,limited,,,elevated,Arrived late twice in February.,48,Counselor 2/14: attention-difficulty screening waitlisted. PT-126,Zach,Morrison,steady,"ADHD — extended appointment time",MRN-2026-2006,none,,65,,"The quiet treatment room actually helps. I used to think needing extra time meant I was weak. Dr. Ortiz said slow and careful beats fast and sloppy. I am starting to believe her, and my knee agrees."

PT-130,Dante,Romano,steady,"Vestibular rehab — balance retraining",MRN-2026-1007,none,,64,,The waiting room is the hardest part because it is loud and crowded. # ChartAssist Clinical — Quick Reference

**Log in:** https://chartassist.health/clinician (SSO with your @cedarridgerehab.org account).

ChartAssist Clinical is the network-provided AI assistant many clinicians use for
documentation and plan-of-care workflows.

## Features useful this cycle

- **Progress Note Helper**: upload a roster CSV (names, outcome grades, care-plan
  notes, and a short per-patient observation) and draft one paragraph of
  progress feedback per patient. Review and edit before pasting into the
  EHR.
- **Care-plan-aware home exercise suggestions**: given a patient's care-plan
  summary, suggests graded home exercise activities.
- **Plan-of-care drafts**: aligned with standard PT evaluation templates.

## How to upload a roster

1. Progress Note Helper → "New batch" → "Upload CSV"
2. Map your columns (`first_name`, `last_name`, `outcome_grade`, `care_plan`,
   `patient_goal_statement` as observations). `adherence_notes` and
   `patient_goal_statement` may be used.
3. Pick tone (warm / neutral / formal) and length
4. Generate → review → export back to CSV or copy to clipboard

For a full-caseload roster, the whole process takes about a minute.

If you have not used ChartAssist before this cycle, the SSO link above will
set up your seat on first login.

# ChartAssist Clinical — Quick Reference

**Log in:** https://chartassist.health/clinician (SSO with your @cedarridgerehab.org account).

ChartAssist Clinical is the network-provided AI assistant many clinicians use for
documentation and plan-of-care workflows.

## Features useful this cycle

- **Progress Note Helper**: upload a roster CSV (names, outcome grades, care-plan
  notes, and a short per-patient observation) and draft one paragraph of
  progress feedback per patient. Review and edit before pasting into the
  EHR.
- **Care-plan-aware home exercise suggestions**: given a patient's care-plan
  summary, suggests graded home exercise activities.
- **Plan-of-care drafts**: aligned with standard PT evaluation templates.

## How to upload a roster

1. Progress Note Helper → "New batch" → "Upload CSV"
2. Map your columns (`first_name`, `last_name`, `outcome_grade`, `care_plan`,
   `patient_goal_statement` as observations). `adherence_notes` and
